# Research

[Draft based on your prior research themes — edit freely.]

### Equity in energy transitions

Globally, nearly 3 billion people cook with traditional stoves and solid fuels, resulting in exposure to household air pollution — the largest energy-related health risk. Our lab studies who benefits from clean energy transitions (e.g., charcoal-to-gas, gas-to-induction) and who is left behind, with attention to gender and intra-household dynamics.

<img src="images/research-1.jpg" style="width:55%" alt=""/>

### Climate, energy, and health disparities in the US

We examine whether shifts away from fossil fuels (e.g., coal-fired power plant retirements) have reduced or reinforced racial/ethnic disparities in health outcomes such as preterm birth.

### Exposure modeling methods

We develop and evaluate methods for estimating personal and long-term exposure to air pollution in settings where ambient monitoring is sparse or a poor proxy for household exposure, including machine learning approaches to non-linear exposure-disparity relationships.
